messages:
zoe: FYI p99 decode spiked ~2x after yesterday's kernel-picker change. Traces point to heavy host-side work (parse/tokenize) + many tiny HTTP/gRPC writes. Also saw KV shard eviction bursts on long prompts.

harry: Do you have a sample trace? Which kernel got chosen for long sequences?

zoe: Quick trace snippet:
```
pprof: host_parse 50% | tokenizer_pool 18% | http2_small_writes 12% | kernel_picker 5% | gpu_kernel_small 4% | kv_evictions 3%
log: req=xyz seq=1100 host_pre=130ms tokenization=38ms grpc_flush=24ms gpu_start_delay=110ms kv_evict=320
```

nina: 1100 tokens going to the small-kernel path is suspicious. We recently switched default to latency-optimized; looks like the picker misclassified some long-seq windows.

harry: Any quick mitigations we can try on canary?

zoe: Proposed quick fixes: 1) pin kernel_picker to `seq_histogram` for longseq routes; 2) re-enable coalesce_writev on ingress to collapse small writes; 3) bump KV shard cap for hot shards (64->128MB) only on canary nodes.

nina: We also found a tokenizer worker change that removed yields; reintroducing a small yield cut run-queue pressure in local replay.

harry: Sounds good. Can you run a 20m replay with the fixes and collect pprof + tcpdump?

zoe: Will do. Repro steps:
```
python tools/replay.py --trace traces/2026-03-25-longseq.json --concurrency 60 --duration 1200 --route longseq-hot
sudo tcpdump -w /tmp/ingress-smallwrites.pcap port 443 and host <ingress-ip>
curl -sS http://localhost:6060/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=30 > /tmp/prof.pb
```

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: canary patch by zoe at 1728454500 (patch includes kernel pin, coalesce_writev=true, kv cap bump for hot shards, tokenizer yield). Monitoring: host_runqueue, http2_small_write_rate, kv_evictions, p99_decode_latency.

zoe: TL;DR: host parsing + disabled writev + picker misclassification -> KV thrash and tail latency. Quick plan = pin + coalesce + targeted kvcap bump + tokenizer yield; follow-up = picker revamp and batching deadline split.
